Retrieve Data from a Metabolites Object

get_data.Rd

Extracts specified data from a Metabolites object for a given data layer. This function allows for optional exclusions of data based on the current @exclusions matrix and supports subsetting by feature and sample IDs.

Usage

get_data(
  metabolites,
  layer,
  feature_ids = NULL,
  sample_ids = NULL,
  drop = FALSE,
  as_df = FALSE
)

Arguments

metabolites

A Metabolites object containing the data to be extracted.

layer

A character string specifying the data layer to extract (e.g., "raw", "post_qc", etc.).

feature_ids

Optional. A vector of row names (features) to extract. Defaults to NULL, meaning all features are included.

sample_ids

Optional. A vector of column names (samples) to extract. Defaults to NULL, meaning all samples are included.

drop

Logical. Whether to drop all NA rows or columns (excluded samples or features)

as_df

Logical. If TRUE, the result is returned as a data.frame; otherwise, the result is returned as a matrix. Default is FALSE.

Value

A matrix (or data.frame, if as_df = TRUE) containing the requested data for the specified layer and subsetting conditions.

Examples

file <- system.file("extdata", "metabolon_v1_example.xlsx", package = "metaboprep2")
metabolites <- Metabolites(project_name = "MYPROJECT",
                           format       = "metabolon_v1",
                           filepath     = file)
metabolites <- import_data(metabolites)
#> Using cached MetaboAnalyst DB.
#> Attempting join [features$hmdb] ~ [annotation$hmdb_id] 
#> Attempting join [features$kegg] ~ [annotation$kegg_id] 
#> Attempting join [features$metabolite_id] ~ [annotation$name] 
#> Attempting join [features$comp_id] ~ [annotation$comp_id] 
#> Warning: 100 unannotated metabolites remain after merging with metabolomics database
metabolites <- metabolite_qc(metabolites, source="raw")
